 WNBA Finals sets another viewership mark in rescheduled Game 3
 by 
 Jon Lewis 
 14 hours ago 
 Share 
 Share 
 Share on X (Twitter) 
 Share on Bluesky 
 Share on Threads 
 Share via Email 
 Copy Link 
 0 
 Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese (5) dribbles during the second half of Game 3 of the WNBA basketball finals against the Golden State Valkyries on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026, in Atlanta. (AP Photo/Brynn Anderson)
 The WNBA Finals set another viewership mark in Game 3. 
 Wednesday’s Valkyries-Dream WNBA Finals Game 3 averaged 1.71 million viewers, combining a Nielsen-measured linear audience on USA Network and CNBC with an Adobe Analytics-measured streaming audience on Peacock — marking the largest audience for Game 3 of the Finals since the winner-take-all Liberty-Comets on NBC in 1999 (3.25M).
 It also ranks as the third-most watched WNBA Finals game ever on cable, behind the winner-take-all Lynx-Liberty Game 5 on ESPN in 2024 (2.15M) and last year’s Mercury-Aces Game 1 (1.86M). Across all networks, it delivered the ninth-largest Finals audience in the history of the event, with two of the series’ first three games ranking in the top ten.
 (Note that out-of-home viewing was not included in Nielsen estimates until 2020 or fully accounted for until 2025, that this is only in the second year of a new Nielsen methodology integrating “Big Data” from smart TVs, set-top boxes and first party data with its traditional panel, and that Nielsen has recently tweaked its measurement to better account for co-viewing of games.)
 Atlanta’s blowout win increased 31% from last year’s Aces-Mercury Game 3 on ESPN (1.30M).
 Game 3 was the first of the WNBA Finals that did not face football competition. Game 1 aired on a college football Saturday and Game 2 opposite NFL “Monday Night Football.” Game 3 was originally scheduled to air opposite NFL “Thursday Night Football,” but was moved up a day to ensure the Dream could play at State Farm Arena in Atlanta, which was occupied Thursday by a Sombr concert.
 The Sombr shuffle put Game 3 in competition with the first full night of the NBA season. ESPN’s competing Timberwolves-Heat game averaged 2.52 million.
 Game 3 was the 12th-straight WNBA Finals game to average a seven-figure audience (2024-present), after the previous 80 had failed to hit the million viewer mark (2003-23). More Finals games have topped the million mark in the past three seasons than in all prior seasons combined (10). (Part of that is owed to the short length of the WNBA Finals in the league’s early days; series were best-of-three until 2005).
 To put the numbers in perspective, Atlanta’s previous WNBA Finals Game 3 — a sweep-clinching loss to Minnesota in 2013 — averaged 321,000 viewers.

 Sports Ratings Tracker SuperMotocross The SMX World Championship Series, including the indoor AMA Supercross Championship and outdoor Pro Motocross Championship, averaged 614,000 viewers on NBC across a Nielsen-measured linear audience and streaming viewership tracked by Adobe Analytics — up 17% from last year. Nielsen updates NBC NFL viewership Nielsen has reprocessed the viewership for NBC’s four NFL games from Week 1-3 of the season. The Patriots-Seahawks Kickoff Game has been updated to 25.2 million, up from an originally-reported 25.1 million. The Week 1 Cowboys-Giants “Sunday Night Football” game has been updated to 25.82 million, up from 25.66 million. Colts-Chiefs the following week has been updated to 24.43 million, up from 24.29 million. Finally, Rams-Broncos in Week 3 has been updated to 20.96 million, up from 20.77 million. WNBA Semis Last Wednesday’s Liberty-Dream WNBA semifinal Game 2 averaged 1.4 million viewers on ESPN, down from Mercury-Lynx in the comparable window last year (1.5M). Last year’s games took place earlier in the calendar and did not face the MLB Postseason. Read more ALDS The MLB American League Division Series was averaging 3.4 million viewers on TNT Sports through Thursday, up 2% from last year’s ALDS on Fox Sports. Last Thursday’s Guardians-White Sox Game 4 averaged 3.8 million opposite NFL “Thursday Night Football,” on par with Brewers-Cubs in the same window last year. Read more Presidents Cup Final round coverage of golf’s Presidents Cup averaged 2.0 million viewers on NBC last Sunday across a Nielsen-measured linear audience (1.1 rating, 1.88M viewers) and streaming viewership tracked by Adobe Analytics — up 37% from the previous edition two years ago and the highest since 2017 (four telecasts). NASCAR “Big Data” NASCAR last week resumed reporting the official Nielsen “Big Data + Panel” ratings and viewership figures for its races, a move that coincides with Nielsen having rolled out a modified version of the methodology at the end of last month. The first race following that decision, Darlington over Labor Day weekend, averaged a 1.0 rating and 1.98 million viewers on USA Network — up 6% and 5% respectively from last year (1.0, 1.9M). Read more Daytona NASCAR Cup Series racing from Daytona averaged a 1.7 rating and 3.12 million viewers on NBC a week ago Saturday, per the “Big Data + Panel” methodology that is the official Nielsen currency, and a 1.8 and 3.51 million under the old “panel-only” metric NASCAR now publicizes for its races.
